absent: Classifier object internals and flow specification match fields and actions.
Receive side scaling context allocation, lookup, and indirection table format.
PHY operation implementations, PLCA state handling, and diagnostic result delivery.
Ethernet base sizes and wire impact of fragment preemption settings.
Netlink extended acknowledgement lifecycle beyond message prefixing.
Eventfd counter update, wait queue, and poll semantics and variant selection.
EVM key handling, verification algorithm, and protection policy for extended attributes.
Executable memory allocation, fallback choice, and mapping protections.
Symbol versioning, namespace enforcement, and module loader use of export records.
Full ext2 superblock layout and block size decoding.
Exception table population and search order for module and BPF entries.
File allocation operation effects and 32 bit translation.

Framebuffer mode programming, blanking levels, pixmap transfer effects, deferred flush timing, and notifier payloads.

findings.text: Two small wrappers describe receive flow classification state. One pairs a pointer to a generic classifier object with trailing variable length private storage owned by the driver. The other pairs a pointer to a flow specification with an integer identifier selecting a receive side scaling context.

Per device ethtool state aggregates an index mapping receive side scaling contexts, a mutex for serializing scaling management, a size value for user provided indirection, and three one bit indicators covering physical identifier busy, wake on LAN enablement, and ongoing module firmware flashing.

The per device state collocates a mutex with scaling context storage and related control fields. The fragments show existence and placement only. They do not show acquisition order, hold times, or which operations take the lock.

A physical layer operations table offers callbacks for querying string set size, fetching descriptive strings, collecting statistics, reading and updating PLCA configuration with extended error reporting, reading PLCA status, and starting cable diagnostics including a time domain variant that takes extra configuration.

Exported helpers translate between an additive preemption fragment count and a minimum size. One direction scales a base Ethernet length by the count. The other searches the permitted minima and returns the matching count.

Minimum size validation accepts only four discrete sizes corresponding to counts zero through three. Other values trigger a module prefixed diagnostic through the netlink error helper and an invalid argument failure. The netlink helper itself prepends the module name to a supplied message.

A string copy helper enforces at build time that the source has the standard ethtool string length, copies that many bytes to the current destination slot, and advances the destination pointer by the same length.

A forced speed descriptor links a numeric speed with a capability mask plus a pointer to a capability array and its length. A companion initializer derives the speed constant and array reference from a shared prefix and value name and fills the length automatically.
Shared creation flags combine close on exec with nonblocking behavior. The full recognized set further includes semaphore mode.

Fallback eventfd helpers provide inert behavior when the feature is unavailable. Lookup by descriptor fails as unimplemented, wait queue removal fails likewise, masked signaling and release and masked read do nothing, and direct signaling delegates to the masked variant with a zero mask.

Two variants gate eventfd signaling. One denies reentrant signaling while the caller is already inside eventfd handling by consulting a per task flag. The other unconditionally permits signaling. The fragments do not show which configuration selects each variant.

EVM entry points report static outcomes without inspecting storage. Attribute list initialization and access control name classification indicate success, while key installation, message authentication repair, and protected attribute retrieval indicate unsupported operation.

EVM status queries use conservative defaults. Cross attribute verification yields unknown, revalidation and metadata change detection yield false, and protected name testing yields false even though its result type is integer.

Executable memory management distinguishes several purpose types sharing a default value for module text, followed by probes, tracing, packet filtering, and module data, terminated by a maximum sentinel. Flags use single bits for shadow memory inclusion and for read only execute caching. Each range records primary and fallback address bounds plus protection, alignment, and flags. A top container holds one range per type.

Module alignment has two forms, plain page size, or page size shifted by the sanitizer shadow scale when that mode applies. Restoration of execute protections and global initialization are inert successes in the shown fragments.

Symbol export helpers emit records carrying a symbol reference, a license tag, and an optional namespace. Layers select between doing nothing, delegating to version tooling, emitting a section record directly, or making the symbol addressable plus optional debug bookkeeping plus inline assembly. Public wrappers cover plain, GPL only, namespaced, namespaced GPL only, and module restricted forms.

Reference emission aligns differently by word size, using eight byte alignment with a quad slot on wider targets and four byte alignment with a long slot on narrower targets. Default namespace handling also varies, supplying either a standard default label or an empty string.
Second extended filesystem ABI fixes name length at 255 and link count at 32000. Superblock displacements place magic at 0x38, block count at 0x04, and block size field at 0x18.

Image size derivation validates the magic field after endian conversion and returns zero on mismatch. On match it multiplies block count by block size derived from the size field through a left shift, both after endian conversion.
Exception table lookups for module and BPF ranges are stubbed to always report no entry.

Space reservation descriptors carry a type, a whence, a start, a length where zero means to end of file, a system identifier, a process identifier, and reserved padding. A 32 bit compatibility twin packs the 64 bit start and length fields while keeping the remaining layout.

Reservation controls use X group numbers 40 through 43 plus 57 for reserve, unreserve, 64 bit reserve, 64 bit unreserve, and zeroing, mirrored for the 32 bit compatibility layout. Mode masking combines allocation, hole punching, range collapse, range zeroing, range insertion, range unsharing, and zeroed writes.

Fault injection probes default to inactive. User copy failure, page allocation failure, slab failure, and generic failure checks all report false, setup reports zero, debugfs attribute creation reports missing device, and config initialization does nothing.

Full fault attributes combine probability and interval with counters for times and space, verbosity, task filtering, stack depth, required and rejected windows, a hit count, rate limit state, and a debugfs name. An initializer supplies interval one, times one, open ended require window, depth 32, disabled rate limiting, verbosity two, and null name, with a declaration macro instantiating the structure. An alternate empty definition carries no fields and uses an empty initializer.
Fault configuration pairs fault attributes with a configuration group in the full form, while the alternate form is empty.
A single fault flag reserves bit zero for suppressing warnings.

Display capability ABI uses powers of two. Power values are 1 for active off, 2 for suspend, 4 for standby. Interface values run 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for digital and four analog variants, then 32, 64, 128, 256 for mono, RGB, multi, and unknown. Signal values are 0 for none, then 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for blank blank, separate, composite, sync on green, and serration. Miscellaneous flags are 1 for primary color, 2 for first detail preferred, 4 for HDMI.

Framebuffer pixmap flags are 1 for default, 2 for system RAM, 4 for iomapped, 256 for DMA capable sync. Blit dimension caps are 64 wide and 128 high. Registration events are 5 for registered and 6 for unregistered. Cursor control is a read write ioctl in F group at number 8 operating on the cursor structure.

Chromaticity storage holds eight fractional values for red, green, blue, and white coordinates. Monitor specifications aggregate that chromaticity with a mode database pointer and length, manufacturer, monitor, serial number, and auxiliary strings, numeric model, serial, year, and week, horizontal and pixel clock minima and maxima, input, power, signal, vertical minima and maxima, gamma, GTF presence, miscellaneous flags, EDID version and revision, and maximum dimensions.

User space color map exchange carries a start, a count, and user pointers for red, green, blue, and optional transparency. User space image exchange carries placement, extent, foreground and background colors for mono, depth, a user data pointer, and an embedded color map descriptor. User space cursor exchange carries selector, enable, raster operation, a user mask pointer, a hot spot, and an embedded image descriptor.

Event delivery pairs a framebuffer handle with opaque data. Blit capability storage pairs two dimension bitmaps with a length and flags. Pixmap storage records an address, size, offset, buffer, scanline, and access alignments, flags, dimension bitmaps, and read and write callbacks. Deferred input tracking records a page with offset plus a private list node, while deferred control records a delay, a sorting option, a page fetch callback, and a handler receiving the collected list.

A framebuffer operations table centralizes driver entry points for open and release, linear read and write, mode validation without touching parameters, mode application, single and batched color programming, blanking, panning, rectangle fill, area copy, image blit, cursor handling, blit synchronization, device specific control including 32 bit compatibility, mapping, capability query, and teardown, with an owner reference.
Framebuffer client registration, unregistration, and notifier invocation are stubbed to immediate success without side effects.

Several layouts demand careful handling. Trailing private storage requires allocation beyond the fixed header. User pointers embedded in color, image, and cursor descriptors require user memory validation with separate compatibility handling for 32 bit layouts. Pixmap dimension bitmaps use width minus one and height minus one indexing. Module alignment differs under sanitizer shadowing, affecting size assumptions.

Fragment size handling forms a tiny search machine that steps through counts zero to three, derives each minimum, compares against the request, and on match records the count and succeeds. If no count matches it emits a diagnostic naming the four legal minima and fails.

Each shown header is protected by a conventional include guard macro that is defined once to prevent multiple inclusion. The fragments show only the guard definitions, not the guarded contents beyond the routed excerpts.
